Saudi Arabia is the kingdom that covers most of the Arabian Peninsula, ruled by the House of Saud, with its capital at Riyadh. It holds Mecca and Medina, the two holiest cities of Islam. The map shows it from 1938.

The Saudi family had built states in Nejd twice before, allied with the teachings of Ibn Abd al-Wahhab. In 1902 the young Ibn Saud retook Riyadh. Over thirty years he conquered central Arabia, the Gulf coast and in 1925 the Hejaz from the Hashemites. In 1932 he named his kingdom Saudi Arabia.

In 1938 American engineers struck oil at Dammam. The oil company that became Saudi Aramco made the kingdom the world's leading oil exporter. Saudi Arabia helped found OPEC in 1960 and led the 1973 oil embargo. It abolished slavery only in 1962.

Every king since Ibn Saud has been one of his sons. The kingdom hosted US troops in the Gulf War of 1991. Since 2017 Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has held real power, opening cinemas and letting women drive while silencing critics.
